subject: general
question: The current population of a town is 50,000. If it is growing at the rate of 6% compounded every year, what will be the population of the town after 2 years?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net percentage growth for 2 years at 6% rate = 6 + 6 + (6 × 6)/100 = 12.36%.

Current **Population** = 50,000.

Total Growth = 12.36% of 50,000 = 0.1236 × 50,000 = 6,180.

Population after 2 years = 50,000 + 6,180 = 56,180.

**∴ The correct answer is 56180.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Current Population (P) = 50,000

Growth Rate (R) = 6% per annum

Time Period (n) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Population after **n** years = P × (1 + R/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/24e2e5aa45a3d475481754ffe165449187dedfec3a42af91aacd567f02144323.png] 

⇒ Population after 1 year = 50,000 × (1 + 6/100)

⇒ Population after 1 year = 50,000 × 1.06 = 53,000

⇒ Population after 2 years = 53,000 × (1 + 6/100)

⇒ Population after 2 years = 53,000 × 1.06

⇒ Population after 2 years = 56,180

**∴ The correct answer is 56180.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value increases by x% and then y% successively, the net percentage change is given by [x + y + (xy/100)]%.

Depreciation Formula

If the population decreases at a rate R, the population after n years is calculated as P × (1 − R/100)ⁿ.

Compound Growth Concept

Growth in **population**, bacteria, or **compound interest** follows the same mathematical model of exponential growth.</p
